chunks: Mountains may move from their position but you should not move from yours.

Grit your teeth. Lend to Allāh your head (in fighting for Allāh, give yourself to Allāh). Plant your feet firmly on the ground. Have your eye on the remotest foe and close your eyes (to their numerical majority). And keep sure that succour is but from Allāh, the Glorified.

key_terms.جُمجُمَتَكَ: Your skull/head (giving oneself completely to God)
key_terms.نَاجِذُكَ: Your canine tooth (biting the tooth signifies gritting teeth in determination)

ai.seo_question: What are the key instructions for steadfastness and battle conduct given by Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this directive to his son Muhammad ibn Hanafiya, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of 'biting the knuckle' (a sign of intense resolve or anxiety) to encourage steadfastness amidst the chaos of the Battle of the Camel. This instruction highlights the Shia emphasis on combining physical preparedness with spiritual reliance (tawakkul), asserting that ultimate victory (nasr) is divinely ordained rather than merely a result of military might. The exhortation serves as a practical guide for leadership, balancing inner composure with outward vigilance.
